sentences.text: Sanxiasaurus is a genus of neornithischian dinosaur, a group of herbivores, named after the Three Gorges of the Yangtze River. The only known species is S. modaoxiensis.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of 55 postcranial bones including vertebrae, forelimbs, hindlimbs, and foot parts.
This animal holds the record as the oldest known neornithischian dinosaur from Asia.
The species name modaoxiensis refers to the Modaoxi tributary where the remains were found.

A fossil bed containing Sanxiasaurus remains was discovered in 2016 in Laojun Village, Yunyang County, by a team from the Chongqing Bureau of Geological and Mineral Resource Exploration and Development. The remains were formally described in 2019 by Chinese paleontologist Ning Li and colleagues as the new taxon Sanxiasaurus modaoxiensis.

Phylogenetic analysis places Sanxiasaurus as a basal neornithischian, more derived than Lesothosaurus but less derived than Hexinlusaurus. A 2024 analysis by André Fonseca and colleagues recovered Sanxiasaurus as more derived than Agilisaurus, potentially placing it in a clade with Hexinlusaurus or leaving its position unresolved.

Sanxiasaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic, approximately 180 to 170 million years ago, in the Aalenian to Toarcian stages. The fossil record for Sanxiasaurus spans from 184.2 to 170.9 million years ago, covering the Toarcian to Aalenian stages.
